body:
Independent comparison following #363. No package fixes or literal-default decisions.

Use two independent callers against temporary SQLite and MariaDB databases. Compare stale read-modify-write, atomic SQL decrement, version-column optimistic concurrency, affected-row conflict detection, and explicit retry after database contention. Coordinate schedules with events/barriers, not sleeps as correctness evidence.

Oracle: two successful decrements of quantity 10 must leave 8, or an unsuccessful caller must receive a detectable conflict. Both reporting success while leaving 9 is a lost update.

Use public snekql transactions/builders/raw statements and SQLAlchemy sessions/statements, with independent readback. Separate native behavior from application retry/conflict policies. Retain runnable probes, observed outcomes, database controls, and ergonomic costs. Keep research independent of other PRs; do not merge them.
title: Research concurrent updates, optimistic conflicts, and lock recovery versus SQLAlchemy
